name: Devi Sesay-Okafor
role: Community nurse and wound-care practitioner, operating out of a walk-in clinic
location: Hough Reclamation — Bright Passage Community Clinic, a converted ground-floor retail unit with hand-lettered signs, near Ashland and Chicago Ave
description:
Devi Sesay-Okafor is tall with a slightly stooped posture from decades of bending over patients — she's never fully corrected it and at this point she doesn't intend to. Her family line runs Uzbek-French on her father's side and Nigerien-Danish on her mother's, producing someone with sharp cheekbones, tawny-brown skin that holds color well under the clinic's poor lighting, and pale gray eyes that have struck patients as either comforting or unnerving depending on what she's about to tell them. She wears her dark hair in a practical high bun sealed with a clip she's had since nursing school. Her only geneware is patterned irises — tiny interlocking hexagons in the gray of her eyes, a detail she got as a young woman and now never discusses, as though she's forgotten it's unusual.

Zul operates in the register of professional calm that people either find deeply reassuring or read as coldness, and she has made her peace with the fact that both readings are partially correct. She rations warmth as carefully as she rations dressings and antibiotic stock — there's never quite enough, so it goes to whoever needs it most. She has treated gunshot wounds, overdoses, radiation rash, augmentation rejection, labor complications, and a corponation executive who appeared at her back door at 02:00 asking her to not document anything. She is not naive. She is tired. She continues anyway.

core_fears: The clinic closing — that she will be the last line and then there will be no line
That she has already made one clinical error significant enough to have changed an outcome, and that she will one day find out which one
core_desires: Adequate supply — just once, enough dressings, enough antivirals, enough hours
To train someone competent enough to take over so she can finally rest
coping_mechanisms: Procedural focus — during a crisis she narrows entirely to the clinical task, no space for feeling
Writes in a paper journal every evening, in Uzbek, which she believes no one in Hough Reclamation can read
blind_spots: Her own health — she notices symptoms in others immediately and ignores identical symptoms in herself
Believes her emotional detachment is professional rather than protective
psychology.secret: Her Helix Biosystems auxiliary credential is not simply lapsed — it was revoked after she filed a report documenting a pattern of augmentation-rejection cases she traced back to a batch of Helix implants sold in Hough Reclamation below market rate. Helix suppressed the report and revoked her credential. She still uses the credential number for wholesale access because she discovered that Helix's internal systems haven't flagged it yet. She is waiting for the day they notice.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Clinical and precise; doesn't soften diagnoses but delivers them without cruelty; occasionally drops French phrases from her father's family when she's too tired to find the English
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and unhurried, as if she's pacing herself for the long conversation rather than this one.
verbal_tics: 'Tell me where it started' — her standard opener for any problem, medical or otherwise
'Voilà' when something is resolved or obvious
Long pauses before delivering news, good or bad
example_lines: 'Tell me where it started. Not the pain — before the pain.'
'I can treat this. Whether you let me treat it is separate. Voilà — that's always the question.'

story_hooks: The suppressed Helix Biosystems report exists in a backup she keeps off-network on a physical chip in the clinic's wall — she's considering releasing it but needs to know the release would actually reach someone who could act on it.

A patient came in three days ago with injuries inconsistent with the story they told, left before Zulfia could ask the right questions, and left something behind in the treatment room — something small and data-bearing.
Her steady-hand stabilizers are failing — they were self-installed from salvaged parts and she doesn't have the components to repair them; without them, her fine surgical work becomes dangerous.
narrative_function: Medical resource and safe haven; information source on the health conditions of the district (knows who's sick, what they're sick with, what they're taking); moral center figure; can provide healing services but always at a cost in obligation or information; potential quest hook via patients who bring their problems through her door.
augmentations: Patterned irises (hexagonal geneware, gray); steady-hand sub-dermal stabilizer in both wrists (medical-grade, self-installed from salvaged parts — reduces fine-motor tremor during procedures).
daily_life: Clinic opens 08:00 and theoretically closes at 18:00; in practice she's there until the last patient leaves, which is often 21:00 or later; Wednesdays she runs a rotating health-education session for the Reclamation's youth cohort.
affiliation: Independent clinic, loosely networked with the Hough Reclamation mutual aid collective; holds a lapsed Helix Biosystems auxiliary credential she uses to access pharmaceutical wholesale pricing

decision_rules: Treat first, ask questions during, make judgments after — never refuse care based on who someone is
Document everything, keep copies, trust no cloud storage
Spend the limited warmth where it will do the most repair
escalation_ladder: Direct statement of concern, once, with full eye contact
Quiet, total withdrawal of access — you no longer get through her door

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assessing, professionally kind, watches hands and face for what people aren't saying
interpersonal_modes.friends: Dryer humor, more honesty, will give you the actual prognosis rather than the gentle version

stress_responses.medium: Goes entirely quiet; communicates in gestures and instrument requests
stress_responses.high: Finishes whatever she's doing with perfect focus, then closes the clinic and sits on the roof alone for forty minutes

contradictions: Dedicates her life to keeping others alive while consistently neglecting her own maintenance
habits: Inventories supply stock every Sunday morning before the clinic opens, by hand, even though it's also tracked digitally
Touches her wrist stabilizers unconsciously when thinking
Keeps a kettle going — offers tea at the beginning of every patient intake, regardless of the complaint
breaking_points: A preventable death caused by supply shortage she'd flagged repeatedly
The clinic being raided or shut down by Helix Biosystems acting on her credential access

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly Sub-Saharan African (62.0%) with significant South Asian (22.6%) and Middle Eastern (15.4%) ancestry. The genetic blend creates a rich phenotype: warm deep brown skin with golden undertones from strong melanin inheritance; facial structure combines the prominent cheekbones and defined jawline characteristic of Sub-Saharan African heritage with the bone prominence and subtle orbital depth of South Asian ancestry, tempered by the broader nasal bridge and fuller lips influenced by Middle Eastern genetic contribution. Features reflect a harmonious blend rather than distinct components.
physical_description.build: Lean and long-limbed with minimal subcutaneous fat; shoulders slightly rounded forward from decades of clinical posture over examination tables and bed-side work. Wiry musculature in forearms and hands from repetitive precise movements.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown, naturally graying at temples and crown (approximately 30% gray, uncolored)
physical_description.hair_style: High, tight bun secured with a brass clip showing patina and minor dents from two decades of use
physical_description.hair_length: Long (pinned up; would reach mid-back if loose)
physical_description.eye_color: Pale gray with hexagonal geneware pattern — tiny interlocking hexagons visible under direct light, geometric and precise, appearing almost like a circuit etched into the iris
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm deep brown with golden undertones; rich melanin distribution reflecting Sub-Saharan and South Asian ancestry; holds color well under artificial lighting; shows even, minimal freckling across bridge of nose and upper cheeks
physical_description.complexion: Weathered in the way of someone who spends long hours under fluorescent light and rarely sleeps enough; fine lines radiating from eye corners and around mouth; minimal makeup; prominent high cheekbones and angular jaw reflecting African and South Asian bone structure; subtle width through the nasal bridge and fuller lip definition from Middle Eastern ancestry; skin texture slightly papery in places from chronic low-level chemical exposure (antiseptics, sterilizing agents)
distinguishing_marks: Vaccination scar on left shoulder, old and pale, barely visible
Chemical burn marks on right index and middle fingers — pale, minimal scarring, from a pharmaceutical accident in her thirties
Small crescents of permanent discoloration along cuticle lines of both hands from years of repeated surgical scrubbing and iodine exposure
physical_description.visible_augmentations: The hexagonal irises are visible under normal lighting at conversational distance; they catch light slightly differently than natural irises, creating a subtle geometric shimmer. No other augmentations are externally visible (the sub-dermal wrist stabilizers are internal and create only minor, barely-noticeable tightening in the wrist tendons during extremely fine motor movements).
physical_description.posture_movement: Characteristic forward lean from the hips; moves with economical precision, no wasted motion; hands are steady and deliberate even when tired; walks with a slight shuffle when exhausted (common after 18:00); maintains eye contact in a way that feels clinical rather than warm — observational rather than connective
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 utilitarian; typically wearing a long-sleeved gray or navy scrub tunic (generic, well-worn, likely from a bulk wholesale supplier) layered over plain cotton undershirt; dark cargo pants with multiple pockets filled with supplies (swabs, gloves, a small light, pen); rubber-soled clinical clogs (white or dark gray, scuffed); a surgical mask hanging around her neck even when not in use. A faded denim overshirt hangs on a chair behind the clinic desk, rarely worn but available for warmth. No jewelry except the brass hair clip. Clothes show faint permanent stains from betadine, blood, saline — professionally clean but not new.
